review.recommendation:
Approve and ship as-is. The round-18 blocking-adjacent question is now closed with direct evidence: `ls CHANGELOG* HISTORY*` returns nothing in the working tree and `git log --oneline --all -- CHANGELOG.md` returns nothing on any branch, so no changelog/version-history convention exists to update; `package.json` version 0.1.0 has demonstrably never been bumped for prior feature ships including `caaa8fe`. The three updated prose surfaces (JIRA_QUEUE.md, embedded `--help` text, and the accepted-post-ship-addition note in the frozen spec) are therefore the complete documentation surface for this contract change.

Re-verified independently from the packet contents this round:
- Fail-safe direction is preserved throughout. `youngestMarkerAgeMs` previously returned `0` for a non-finite now, an unparseable marker timestamp, or a non-finite age — a value that always compared below the floor and therefore blocked. It now returns `null` for those cases plus negative (future-dated) ages, and both call sites treat `null` as blocking (`preMutationDuplicateGate` via an explicit `youngestMarkerAge === null` early return; `runVerification` via `markerAgeMeasurable` in the `canClear` conjunction). No input that previously blocked can now clear.
- `gateExitCode()` is strictly narrowing: exit 20 is reachable only when `gate.keys` is empty/absent AND `gate.reason === VERIFICATION_REASON.INDEX_LAG`, and that reason is assigned at exactly one return site — the measurable-age-below-floor branch. Poll exhaustion, search failure, and unmeasurable age all carry `SEARCH_UNAVAILABLE`/`MARKER_AGE_UNMEASURABLE` and fall through to exit 2, matching both prose surfaces and the `keeps poll exhaustion and search failure at exit 2` test.
- The duplicate branch is unchanged: `keys?.length` still short-circuits to `EXIT.DUPLICATE` before any reason inspection, so the pre-existing duplicate contract is untouched.
- The persisted-audit-reason concern from round 17 is genuinely closed rather than argued away. The only `.reason` branch in the file (line 1087) reads `gate.reason`, the in-memory return of `preMutationDuplicateGate()` within the same invocation, not a persisted `audit[].reason`. Existing on-disk drafts carrying the old `marker-younger-than-index-lag-minimum` string in unmeasurable-age cases remain valid and unread by any branch.
- Exit-inventory integrity is asserted mechanically, not just by prose: the test pins `EXIT.STATE_ERROR === 2`, `EXIT.INDEX_LAG_BLOCKED === 20`, the full sorted inventory, and the absence of retired codes 10–12. 20 is a safe numeric choice — outside the shell-reserved 126/127/128+ range and colliding with nothing in the inventory.
- Scope discipline holds. `VERIFY_CLEAR_MIN_AGE_FLOOR_MS` is confirmed hard-coded at 30000 with `state.poll.minimumDurationMs` reachable only via test injection and, through `Math.max`, capable only of raising the effective minimum. That is pre-existing shipped behavior recorded as an accepted spec deviation; this addition changes only which code is returned when the pre-existing floor blocks, not the floor itself. Correctly left alone.

One optional, explicitly non-blocking polish for a future touch — do not gate this ship on it: the in-memory gate vocabulary (`'index-lag'`) differs from the persisted audit vocabulary (`'marker-younger-than-index-lag-minimum'`) for the same physical condition, so a maintainer grepping `index-lag` will hit the gate constant and the audit constant with no obvious link between them. A one-line comment at the `VERIFICATION_REASON` declaration noting that `INDEX_LAG` is an exit-code routing token never persisted to audit, while the other three are persisted audit strings, would remove the ambiguity at zero risk.
review.strongestObjection: The one residual that repository-internal evidence structurally cannot close is an out-of-repo consumer of this plugin, installed elsewhere, that branches on exit code 2 for the index-lag case and will now receive 20. No amount of in-repo grepping can observe that population, so the round-19 "no consumers found" verdict is sound for this repository but silent about installed copies. It is nonetheless not ship-blocking: 20 is nonzero, so any generic `code !== 0` or `if (!ok)` handling is unaffected, and the only consumer that breaks is one performing an exact `=== 2` comparison specifically to detect this narrow gate case — a discrimination the old shared code made impossible to express reliably in the first place, since exit 2 conflated index lag with poll exhaustion, search failure, unmeasurable marker age, and every other wrong-state invocation. Such a consumer could not have been correct before the change, so the realistic blast radius is a consumer that was already misclassifying, and the failure direction is a refusal to proceed rather than a silent duplicate ticket. The owner has explicitly accepted this residual across prior rounds and it is disclosed in the spec note.
